title: Protective effect and mechanism of synagrantol A from Euphorbia pseudomollis on LPS-induced neuroinflammation.
authors: Hu, Qingwen; Zhang, Dan; Wang, Hanxuan; Chen, Keyuan; Zhang, Fuyuan; Zhang, Xin; Zhu, Yi Zhun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物化合物A3对LPS诱导神经炎症的保护作用，涉及分子对接但核心为炎症表型与信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Species of Euphorbia (Euphorbiaceae) have traditionally been utilized worldwide for analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer applications. Latex and extracts from these plants have long been used in Brazilian indigenous medicine. The utilization of contemporary extraction and analytical methodologies to clarify the anti-inflammatory pharmacology of Euphorbia extracts establishes a translational connection between conventional knowledge and modern drug discovery. AIM OF THE STUDY: Neuroinflammation plays a significant role in the pathogenesis of various neurological disorders. 3,4,12,13-Tetraacetyl-20-phenylacetylphorbol (synagrantol A, referred to as A3), a novel compound isolated from Euphorbia pseudomollis Bruyns (syn. Synadenium molle Pax), a shrub indigenous to East Africa, has been previously documented for its anti-inflammatory properties. The purpose of this research was to examine whether A3 could both in vitro and in vivo regulate LPS-induced neuroinflammation. METHODS: The chemical constituents of the plant extracts were characterized using UPLC, LC-MS, QTOF, and NMR technologies. In vitro, BV2 microglial cells were pretreated with A3 followed by LPS stimulation. Cell viability (CCK-8), nitric oxide (NO) production, inflammatory cytokine expression, and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) levels were assessed. RNA-seq was performed at 1 h and 4 h post-LPS stimulation. Direct compound-target interactions were evaluated through cellular thermal shift assays and molecular docking analyses. In vivo, mice received daily intraperitoneal LPS injections for 7 days, with or without A3 treatment (5 or 15 mg/kg). Behavioral assessments included the open field test (OFT). Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and splenic metrics were analyzed. RESULTS: The UPLC-QTOF-LC/MS-NMR analysis showed that 3,4,12,13-Tetraacetyl-20-phenylacetylphorbol was the essential component in the ethanol extracts of Euphorbia pseudomollis Bruyns. In vitro, A3 reduced LPS-induced NO production and iNOS expression in BV2 cells in a dose-dependent manner, while maintaining cell viability. RNA-seq revealed more differentially expressed genes at 4 h than at 1 h, with GSEA at both time points implicating the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. In vivo, A3 ameliorated LPS-induced weight loss, hypothermia, and physical deterioration. OFT showed reduced anxiety-like behavior and improved locomotor activity. Histological analyses demonstrated attenuated hippocampal neuronal loss, suppressed microglial activation, and reduced peripheral organ pathology, including splenomegaly. CONCLUSION: A3 demonstrates significant anti-neuroinflammatory effects by inhibiting microglial activation, reducing inflammatory mediators, and downregulating NF-kappaB-associated gene expression, while also mitigating behavioral and pathological impairments in LPS-induced animals.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：大戟属（Euphorbia）植物在全球范围内传统上被用于镇痛、抗炎和抗癌用途。这些植物的乳汁和提取物长期用于巴西土著医学。利用现代提取和分析方法阐明大戟提取物的抗炎药理学，在传统知识与现代药物发现之间建立了转化联系。研究目的：神经炎症在多种神经系统疾病的发病机制中发挥重要作用。3,4,12,13-四乙酰基-20-苯乙酰基佛波醇（synagrantol A，简称A3），一种从原产于东非的灌木 Euphorbia pseudomollis Bruyns（同义词 Synadenium molle Pax）中分离出的新化合物，先前已有文献记载其抗炎特性。本研究旨在探讨A3是否能在体外和体内调节LPS诱导的神经炎症。方法：使用UPLC、LC-MS、QTOF和NMR技术对植物提取物的化学成分进行表征。体外实验中，BV2小胶质细胞先用A3预处理，随后进行LPS刺激。评估细胞活力（CCK-8）、一氧化氮（NO）产生、炎症细胞因子表达和诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）水平。在LPS刺激后1小时和4小时进行RNA-seq。通过细胞热位移分析和分子对接分析评估直接的化合物-靶点相互作用。体内实验中，小鼠连续7天接受每日腹腔注射LPS，伴或不伴A3治疗（5或15 mg/kg）。行为评估包括旷场实验（OFT）。分析组织病理学、免疫组织化学和脾脏指标。结果：UPLC-QTOF-LC/MS-NMR分析显示，3,4,12,13-四乙酰基-20-苯乙酰基佛波醇是 Euphorbia pseudomollis Bruyns 乙醇提取物中的关键成分。体外实验中，A3以剂量依赖性方式降低LPS诱导的BV2细胞中NO产生和iNOS表达，同时维持细胞活力。RNA-seq显示4小时时差异表达基因多于1小时，两个时间点的GSEA均涉及NF-kappaB信号通路。体内实验中，A3改善了LPS诱导的体重减轻、体温过低和身体状态恶化。OFT显示焦虑样行为减少和运动活性改善。组织学分析显示海马神经元损失减轻、小胶质细胞活化受到抑制，以及外周器官病理（包括脾肿大）减轻。结论：A3通过抑制小胶质细胞活化、减少炎症介质和下调NF-kappaB相关基因表达，同时减轻LPS诱导动物的行为和病理损伤，展现出显著的抗神经炎症效应。
